summary: A class describes what data and methods an object has. You create objects from the class and each one keeps its own copy of the data.
notes: self.name = name inside __init__ creates the name field on the new object.
maya.add_score(92) passes maya as self automatically. You never pass self yourself.
average() checks for an empty list first, because sum([]) / 0 raises ZeroDivisionError.
pitfall: Forgetting self in a method header, like def add_score(score), causes TypeError: Student.add_score() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given.
